question.text: The Data Management Plan should clearly articulate how the PI and co-PIs plan to manage

json.answer:
and disseminate data generated by the project. The plan should outline the rights and
obligations of all parties as to their roles and responsibilities in the management and

question.text: retention of research data, and consider changes that would occur should a PI or co-PI

json.answer: leave the institution or project. Any costs should be explained in the Budget Justification

question.text: Data will be generated at each of our institutional sites. The PI at each institution will be responsible

json.answer:
for following the data management guidelines described below, and for saving the data to the RIC
servers. This process of transferring all data to a central location will be facilitated by our research

question.text: project coordinator. Our data management guidelines will be reviewed at the kickoff meeting for the

json.answer: project, and revisited briefly at each of our quarterly meetings with the PIs.

question.text: The Data Management Plan should describe the types of data, samples, physical

json.answer:
collections, software, curriculum materials, or other materials to be produced in the course
of the project. It should then describe the expected types of data to be retained and shared,

question.text: and the plans for doing so. The DMP should cover how data are to be managed and

json.answer: maintained during the project.

section.title: We will manage all scientific and technical content generated from this proposal. Our products will

question.text: include 3 broad types of data.

json.answer:
First, we will have data related to each of our proposed experiments. These will include the detailed
protocols used for each experiment, the raw data collected from each experiment, and the

question.text: experimental code used to collect those data. The relevant code will include both the data acquisition

json.answer: code, and the code for the controllers used in the experiment. Together, this information will be

section.title: sufficient for recreating the circumstances of each data collection session.

question.text: Our second type of data will be the code and results for all analyses completed on experimental data.

json.answer:
Specifically, we store all code necessary to recreate figures, tables, and other results reported in all
published manuscripts.

question.text: The proposed foundational developments will produce substantial simulation code for controller

json.answer: development and testing. These and the outputs relevant to all key findings will also be managed.

section.title: Policies for access and sharing and appropriate protection and privacy

question.text: The Data Management Plan should describe the period of time the data will be retained

json.answer:
and shared; factors that limit the ability to manage and share data, e.g., legal and ethical
restrictions on access to human subjects data; and provisions for appropriate protection of

question.text: privacy, confidentiality, security, and intellectual property.

json.answer: Data will be made available upon request, after the conclusion of each of study. The availability of

section.title: data (raw and analyzed) will be advertised on the project’s website. Access will be free, but the

question.text: original data collector/creator/principal investigator retains the right to use the data for analysis

json.answer:
before making it publicly available. No patient identifying information will be included in any of the
available data files.

question.text: Select videos of the experiments will be distributed, with subject faces blurred so as to be

json.answer: unidentifiable. Experimental analyses results will be made available through peer-reviewed journal

section.title: publications and conference presentations. The code needed to generate all published results will be

question.text: documented clearly.

json.answer:
Software generated under the project will be released under the GNU Public License, and available
for free download on the labs’ websites. This includes code for each of our 3 experimental systems.

question.text: We commit to speaking with any qualified scientist who wishes to discuss our results or the

json.answer: technology employed to obtain our results.

section.title: There will be no copyright or licensing required for any of the data generated in this project.

question.text: Research records will be archived for a minimum of seven years after final reporting or publication

json.answer:
of a project. If any questions regarding the research, including but not limited to research integrity
allegations, are raised during the seven- year retention period, the PI will keep the records until such

question.text: questions are fully resolved.

json.answer: Data storage and preservation of access

section.title: The Data Management Plan should describe the mechanisms and formats for storing data

question.text: and making them accessible to others, which may include third party facilities and

json.answer:
repositories; and other types of information that would be maintained and shared regarding
data, e.g. the means by which it was generated, detailed analytical and procedural

question.text: information required to reproduce experimental results, and other metadata.

json.answer: The servers at the Rehabilitation Institute of Chicago will serve as the central repository for all

section.title: collected data. Raw data files will be saved in either Matlab or comma-separated value (CSV)

question.text: format. Code for converting between these formats will also be provided to ensure easy access. The

json.answer:
contents of each data file, including the experimental conditions or the analysis procedures used
during generation will be documented. All raw data will be de-identified to ensure subject

question.text: anonynimity.

json.answer: Upon request, data will be made available through the project's website, hosted on an archived server

section.title: run by the RIC IT Team.
